description: Add Factory-configured outbound webhooks that subscribe to the existing canonical Factory Event stream and POST signed Work state-transition and dispatch-failure envelopes with filtering, bounded retry/backoff, and durable dead-letter logging. The feature lets external monitors react without polling while preserving Recordings as the event authority and keeping delivery failure isolated from Factory Runtime state.

context.customerAsk: Factory configuration declares webhook endpoints with an event filter; the server POSTs a signed JSON envelope on Work state transitions and dispatch failures, retries receiver failures with backoff, retains exhausted deliveries in a dead-letter log, and proves transition delivery, filtering, retry, and disabled behavior with a local test HTTP receiver.
context.problem: Operators currently poll Work state and independently reconstruct transitions and failures even though the engine already records those facts in its canonical Factory Event stream. This adds latency and load and leaves external integrations without authenticated, reliable push delivery.
context.solution: Add validated webhook declarations to Factory definitions and an asynchronous outbound subscriber over the Recordings-owned canonical event stream. Send the unchanged canonical event envelope with timestamped HMAC-SHA256 signing, filter using existing event types and dispatch statuses, retry transient failures with bounded exponential backoff, and append terminal failures to a redacted session-owned dead-letter log without mutating or blocking Factory execution.

acceptanceCriteria: A Factory definition can declare named webhook endpoints with enabled, url, signingSecretRef, canonical eventTypes, canonical dispatchStatuses, and bounded delivery policy fields; invalid names, URLs, secret references, filters, or retry values fail Factory definition validation with actionable field-level findings.

An enabled endpoint receives the exact canonical Factory Event JSON envelope for each matching WORK_STATE_CHANGE, with HMAC-SHA256 signature and timestamp headers that a receiver can independently verify from the configured secret and exact request bytes.

Dispatch failures are selected from existing DISPATCH_RESPONSE, DISPATCH_RECONCILED, and DISPATCH_INTERRUPTED events using their canonical payload status; no new failure event kind or runtime state transition is introduced, nonmatching events are omitted, and disabled endpoints receive no requests.

Retryable transport failures, HTTP 408/429 responses, and HTTP 5xx responses retry with bounded exponential backoff; success stops retrying, non-retryable HTTP responses and exhausted retries produce one redacted dead-letter record, and delivery failure never changes or blocks canonical Factory Session or Work state.

Functional coverage uses a local test HTTP receiver and deterministic synchronization/time to prove transition delivery, filter behavior, receiver-failure retry, signed-body verification, dead-letter exhaustion, and no delivery when disabled.
Typecheck, focused and functional tests pass; no NEW lint violations relative to current main, and the gates green on main (backend-size, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, pkg-structure, vet) stay green.

The implementation/review loop continues until required CI is terminal and passing, all blocking PR conversation feedback is explicitly addressed, merge conflicts and shared/generated-file contention are resolved against current main, and the PR is actually merged.

userStories.title: Declare and validate webhook subscriptions
userStories.description: As a Factory author, I want to declare secure, filtered webhook endpoints in the Factory definition so outbound delivery behavior is explicit and invalid subscriptions are rejected before a run.
acceptanceCriteria: A Factory definition accepts a webhooks collection whose entries have a unique nonempty name, enabled, an absolute http or https url, a nonempty signingSecretRef, and a filter containing at least one supported canonical eventTypes value: WORK_STATE_CHANGE, DISPATCH_RESPONSE, DISPATCH_RECONCILED, or DISPATCH_INTERRUPTED.
The optional canonical dispatchStatuses filter accepts only FAILED and INTERRUPTED, applies only to dispatch event types, and does not introduce a synthetic DISPATCH_FAILURE event name.

Delivery policy supports requestTimeout, maxAttempts including the initial attempt, initialBackoff, backoffMultiplier, and maxBackoff; omitted values resolve to 10 seconds, 5 attempts, 1 second, 2.0, and 30 seconds respectively.

Structural and effective Factory validation rejects duplicate endpoint names, unsupported URL schemes, empty secret references, empty or incompatible filters, and nonpositive or internally inconsistent delivery values with the endpoint name and failing field in the finding.
Definition loading, cloning, compilation, persistence/readback, and any exposed/generated Factory contract preserve webhook declarations without exposing resolved secret values.
Existing Factory definitions without webhooks retain their current behavior and start no outbound subscriber work.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Implemented the Factory webhook declaration contract, generated API/schema mappings, default delivery-policy resolver, structural/effective validation, secret-reference-only handling, clone preservation, and focused round-trip/default/validation coverage. Backend and UI typechecks plus Factory Definitions, HTTP, mapping, and contract verification pass.

userStories.title: Deliver signed Work state-transition events
userStories.description: As an external monitor, I want authenticated Work transition events pushed to my endpoint so I can react without polling or reconstructing another event format.
acceptanceCriteria: During an active Factory Session, every canonical WORK_STATE_CHANGE emitted after webhook activation is delivered once to each enabled endpoint whose filter matches it; endpoint filters are evaluated independently.

The HTTP POST body is the unchanged canonical Factory Event envelope, including its existing schema version, event ID, type, context, ordering/correlation data, and payload; delivery metadata does not replace or rename canonical event fields.

Requests use Content-Type application/json, an event-ID header, a Unix timestamp header, and a versioned HMAC-SHA256 signature header computed over <timestamp>.<exact request body bytes> using the runtime-resolved secret.

Secret material is resolved through an injected secret boundary, is never stored in the Factory Event, dead-letter body, or routine logs, and a missing secret produces an actionable endpoint delivery failure without preventing Factory execution.
A 2xx receiver response marks the delivery successful and causes no retry; receiver response bodies are bounded and are not copied into canonical Factory history.

Subscriber lifecycle follows Factory Session/process activation and shutdown, uses the Recordings service's canonical subscription contract, and does not create a second event producer, taxonomy, or canonical ledger.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Implemented session-scoped canonical Recordings subscriptions for enabled endpoints, activation cursors, exact Factory Event envelope POSTs, injected secret/HTTP/clock effects, v1 HMAC signing headers, request timeouts, bounded response-body consumption, independent endpoint workers, disabled-endpoint no-op behavior, missing-secret isolation, and runtime cleanup ownership. Added local HTTP receiver, signature, filter, disabled, missing-secret, and response-bound tests.

userStories.title: Filter and deliver canonical dispatch failures
userStories.description: As an operator, I want endpoints to receive only the dispatch failures they selected so alerting is useful without success-event noise or a parallel failure model.
acceptanceCriteria: A DISPATCH_RESPONSE or DISPATCH_RECONCILED qualifies as a dispatch failure only when its canonical result/status field is FAILED; a DISPATCH_INTERRUPTED qualifies when its canonical observed status/filter match identifies INTERRUPTED.

Matching dispatch failure requests retain the original canonical event type, payload failure detail, event ID, dispatch ID, Work IDs, Factory Session identity, sequence, and event time; the subscriber does not synthesize a DISPATCH_FAILURE event.
An endpoint receives no event whose type or dispatch status is absent from its filter, including successful dispatch responses and unrelated Factory events.
A disabled endpoint performs no secret resolution, network request, retry scheduling, or dead-letter write, even when matching canonical events occur.
Multiple matching endpoints are isolated so a slow or failing receiver does not delay delivery attempts to another endpoint or Factory Runtime progress.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Extended the session-scoped Webhooks subscriber to match canonical dispatch failures without introducing a synthetic event: DISPATCH_RESPONSE outcome FAILED, DISPATCH_RECONCILED reconciledStatus FAILED, and DISPATCH_INTERRUPTED observedStatus INTERRUPTED. Dispatch status filters are honored, omitted status filters select only the event type's failure status, successful/unrelated events are omitted, and original canonical envelopes are delivered unchanged. Added local HTTP receiver coverage for all three failure event types, status filtering, nonmatching successes, event identity/type/payload preservation, and default failure selection. Focused, race, lifecycle/wire, structure, and full short Go tests pass.

userStories.title: Retry failures and retain dead letters
userStories.description: As an operator, I want transient receiver failures retried and terminal failures retained so webhook outages are diagnosable without corrupting or stalling Factory work.
acceptanceCriteria: Network and timeout errors, HTTP 408, HTTP 429, and HTTP 5xx responses are retryable; other HTTP 4xx responses are terminal after the first attempt, and any 2xx response completes delivery.

Retry delays follow the endpoint's bounded exponential policy, never exceed maxBackoff, honor a valid Retry-After value for 429/503 without exceeding the configured bound, and are driven by an injected clock/scheduler for deterministic tests and cancellation.

Every attempt reuses the same canonical event ID and body, generates a current timestamp/signature, records structured endpoint/event/attempt/outcome diagnostics, and does not log secrets or unrestricted receiver response bodies.

After a non-retryable response or maxAttempts exhaustion, exactly one append-only JSON-lines dead-letter record is retained in session-owned runtime storage with endpoint name, destination origin/path, canonical event ID/type/context, attempt count, timestamps, terminal reason/status, and the canonical body or a lossless safe reference sufficient for manual replay; secret values and sensitive response bodies are excluded.
Dead-letter append failure is surfaced through structured operational diagnostics while canonical Factory Session and Work state continue unaffected.

A functional test constructed through root.BuildProcess and Process.Execute uses a local HTTP receiver plus deterministic observation/time to prove transition delivery, filtering, signature verification, retry then success, retry exhaustion/dead-letter output, and disabled no-delivery without sleep-based polling.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
userStories.notes: Implemented bounded retry/backoff with Retry-After and cancellation, fresh signed attempts over the unchanged canonical envelope, redacted session-owned JSONL dead letters, nonblocking append diagnostics, and canonical session metadata propagation for scoped operator Work transitions. Reconnects bounded subscription gaps from Recordings' last-delivered cursor, restricts HTTP server retries to 500-599, and selects durable filesystem behavior only from the canonical platform wire.
